name: Māra's deeds against the perfection of wisdom
description: Slowness or scattering of eloquence, yawning and laughing while copying, weariness, turning to lesser sūtras, false visions of the Buddha denying the teaching.

name: The four Māras
description: Māra as the aggregates, the defilements, death, and the divine son Māra.
notes: Standard Mahāyāna list (e.g. in the Lalitavistara and Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra); exact sūtra locus not asserted.

name: The fifty demonic states of the aggregates
description: States arising as each aggregate is penetrated in meditation — visions, lights, excessive compassion, boldness, elation, false views of nirvāṇa, possession-like states — which lead astray if taken as sagehood.
antidotes: not taking the state as sagehood

name: Relishing the taste of meditation without skillful means
description: Savoring dhyāna and samādhi without skillful means is the bodhisattva's bondage.

name: Falling to the level of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas
description: For a bodhisattva, realizing the reality-limit before his roots are ripe or lacking wisdom and skillful means — like a wingless bird or an unbaked pot.

name: Fear on hearing the profound teaching
description: Being frightened when hearing that all dharmas are empty and like illusions.

name: Rejecting the true dharma (saddharmapratikṣepa)
description: Denying that the Mahāyāna sūtras are the Buddha's word; a karma worse than the five deadly acts, excluded from the eighteenth vow, and the mark of the icchantika.

name: The view of emptiness (śūnyatādṛṣṭi)
description: Taking emptiness itself as a view or as annihilation — 'incurable', worse than a view of self as large as Sumeru; the RGV criticizes those 'distracted about emptiness'.

name: The four notions (self, being, soul, person)
description: Notions whose presence means one is not a bodhisattva.

name: The four inversions (and the Mahāyāna double set)
description: Taking the impermanent, suffering, selfless and impure as permanent, blissful, self and pure; in the Mahāparinirvāṇa and Śrīmālā also taking the Tathāgata's permanence, bliss, self and purity as their opposites.
notes: The first set of four is shared with the Pali vipallāsa (AN 4.49); the reversed set is the Mahāyāna Mahāparinirvāṇa's and Śrīmālā's addition.

name: The five faults removed by the buddha-nature teaching
description: Discouragement, contempt for inferior beings, grasping the unreal, denying the real dharma, excessive self-love.

name: The five turbidities (pañcakaṣāya)
description: Degeneracy of the aeon, beings, defilements, views and lifespan, in which the Buddha teaches by skillful means.

name: Pride and conceit (abhimāna)
description: Claiming attainments not reached (the five thousand who left the Lotus assembly); bodhisattvas' anger and contempt toward one another.

name: The ground (entrenchment) of ignorance (avidyāvāsabhūmi)
description: The beginningless subtle ignorance remaining in arhats and pratyekabuddhas, removed only by buddhas.
